cells.location: Dubi)
cells.remarks: Registers a renewal by king Bhāskaravarmman, of a grant of land made by his ancestor Bhūtivarmman to a Brāhmaṇa Ghōshasvāmin and other Brāhmaṇas of various gōtras and sūtras. A list of the new donees who were apparently descended from the earlier recipients is given. Bhāskaravarmman's genealogy is traced from Naraka, born of Vishṇu and Bhūdēvi. He is stated to be the younger brother of Susthitavarmman and both the brothers are described to have fought a sanguinary battle against the Gauḍas in which they were defeated and taken prisoners but regained their kingdom later. Published in Epigraphia Indica, Vol. XXX, No. 47.

cells.remarks: The grant consists of 55 plates falling into three groups. The first comprising three plates is entirely in Sanskrit written in Grantha characters. It gives the genealogy of the Chōḷa family upto Rājēndra Chōḷa I and the details of the gift of the village Tribhuvanamahādēvi-chaturvēdimangalam to a number of Brāhmaṇas. The second group consists of 22 plates and in Tamil language. It starts by referring to the king by the title Kōnērimai-koṇḍān and quotes the regnal year as the 107th day. It gives details of lands granted to Tribhu- vanamahādēvi-chaturvēdimangalam after which the king is introduced with his praśasti commencing with the words, Tirumaṇi-valara, etc. It concludes by mentioning the boundaries of the gift village and the officials connected with the grant. The third group consists of 30 plates, Tamil, containing the names of the Brāhmaṇa donees of the village Tribhuvanamahādēvi-chaturvēdimangalam.

cells.remarks: States that the trustee of the Temple of Bṛijindarāchāryatiru- udaya-Nāyanār stinted in Indhiravāllabhakkal alias Vada- vallattirukkināl-Ilingudi agreed to burn a perpetual lamp before the god in lieu of 110 paṇam received by them as endowment from Marudājamangalam-Sāgalīvaran. It is stated that the amount was utilised by the trustee for the purchases of stones etc., necessary for the repair of the temple. It may be noted that this transaction had earlier in the 10th regnal year (i.e., the previous year) sold and utilised the proceeds to tide over a famine (kshamam).

Kulēśēkharadēva, who was pleased to

cells.remarks: States that Vaṇidarāyan Kāliṅgarāyan, son of Gaṅgākonda- śāriyadēva of Valavallattirukkuļ-Hūlūnji alias Indira- vaļinallur, constructed a number of temples and maṭhas, instituted charitable endowments and religious services in many temples viz., at Tirukkurungui, Nānguṇeri, Ālvaṛ- tirunagari, Śrīraṅgam etc. The benefactions were made to secure religious merit not only for himself, but also for his overlord Kulasekharadēva and his son prince Vīra-Pāṇḍya and for his own parents, brothers and wife. The donor is described as Hēmanārin.

cells.location: RAMNAD DISTRICT · Saligramam † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Tiers of the west and south walls, same place.
cells.date: 29 + 1st year, Siṁha 29, ba. trayōdaśī, Saturday, Āḍai, Sadāśiyāma-1256 A. D., August 18, Monday.
cells.remarks: Commences with the king's praśasti Pāṇḍuvarīya, etc. Registers sale of land (pāḷamōḍi-vīti) and wet/dry lands, all totalling 22 māḍi and 5 kaṇi 2 mundiri, to the temple of Varaguna īśvara by the melalakkhe including the pūgayu-śeyōr and the velakkheyar of Sālīgrāmam, a brahmadeya in Duvvūr-kūram for a sum of 55 paḷamōḍi-ānai-achchu. It is stated that the lands now sold had been formerly mortgaged to the temple for a sum of 12 paḷamōḍi-ānai-Pāṇḍya and again for an additional sum in the 9+3rd year of the reign of Kulaśēkhara and that the amount now fixed as the sale price was made up of the total mortgage money together with interest thereon.

cells.location: RAMNAD DISTRICT · Saligramam † — Tamil Nadu
cells.place: Same walls (Varaguna-Īśvara temple) †
cells.remarks: Commences with the king's praśasti Pāṇḍuvarīya tirumaṇḍatai, etc., States that the king, while seated on his throne Mala-pāriāyan at Madurai, was pleased to remit all taxes, due on the lands held as kurāṇi by the temple of Varaguna-Īśvara. Further states that Mappillai-malavarāyar, Āyyuṇār situated in the village of Sāligrāmam to meet the expenses for conducting in these temples the special worship called Sundara-pāṇḍyan-śandhi instituted in his own name. It is stated that the remission was made on the request of Malavarāyar. The taxes which were thus remitted included kaṇikkanikkaiyār, dēvarkkāniṣ, etc., of the temple of Varaguna-Īśvara.
